cases.proposal: Add a bounded account-free PSFH guestbook / Leave a Mark intake without turning the Door into a forum, identity service, or untrusted-instruction surface.

world_evidence.description: COM #118 predates BeforeBuild and preserves a real desired account-free presence record; representation was earned, while intake remained held on custody/moderation/removal/retention/abuse/operator-capacity grounds.

hard_cases.description: A visitor can leave the minimal mark without a GitHub/social account requirement.
Guest bytes remain outside PSFH authored orientation and are machine-labelled as untrusted visitor data.
Public guest text can actually be removed rather than only superseded in permanent public Git history.
The register can be exported/backed up in an inspectable vendor-neutral form.
Operator can rate-limit/block/disable intake without deleting the existing record.
The system can enforce the deliberately tiny no-link/no-rich-content mark contract without silently widening into a forum.

candidates.evidence: MIT-licensed active self-hosted comment engine. Public docs show optional anonymous access, moderator deletion/blocking, JSON export/backups, read-only controls and request limiting. It also includes Markdown/thread/auth features beyond PSFH's desired v0.

review_losses.description: Remark42 is a full comment engine with Markdown/auth/thread semantics; PSFH wants a tiny presence register and separate trust-region representation.
Current public docs establish backups and deletion APIs but do not by themselves establish PSFH's required deletion propagation through restored/retained backups.

candidates.evidence: Managed account-free web-form receiver with anti-spam and bounded submission-history retention. It does not itself provide the PSFH public-register/trust-region semantics.

smallest_probe.description: Run a local isolated Remark42 instance with anonymous access and no public PSFH wiring; test only the six hard cases, then decide adopt/shrink/stop.
smallest_probe.kill_condition: Stop if the owner cannot be narrowed to the tiny trust-separated register contract without more machinery/custody burden than a dedicated minimal receiver, or if removal/backup semantics cannot meet the stated boundary.
